summary: Brian compares quantum-computing ETFs after a wave of quantum IPOs, headlined by Honeywell's record listing, ranking three funds and warning against a fourth. His #3 is QTUM (Defiance, $5B+, 0.40% fee) — 'barely a quantum fund,' with only 4-6% pure-play exposure since it tracks a machine-learning index dominated by Micron, Intel and Palantir. His #1 is WQTM (WisdomTree, 0.45%), genuinely pure-play with IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave and Quantum Computing Inc as its four largest holdings — four different physics approaches (trapped ion, superconducting, annealing, photonics) — though young and volatile. His #2 is CQTM (0.35%, actively managed, ~18 names), the cheapest and most concentrated at ~60% pure-play with IonQ and D-Wave near half the fund, plus post-quantum security exposure — but only weeks old. He warns hard against QPUX, the 2x leveraged daily-reset fund: $1,000 invested before the last pullback became ~$180, a 'falling guillotine' unsuitable for holding, on top of a 1.29% fee. For individual stocks, he holds all four pure plays — IonQ (IONQ, HOLD), Rigetti (RGTI, HOLD), D-Wave (QBTS, HOLD) and Quantum Computing Inc (QUBT, HOLD) — as a deliberate 2.5%-of-portfolio 'asymmetric lane': $1,000 in each two years ago would be ~$84,000 today. He explains the four technologies are not the same bet, which is the entire rationale for a basket. His closing rule: don't buy the label, buy what's inside. A sponsored Telescope Innovations segment is included.
title: I Made 20x on Quantum! This Is the Fund I'd Buy
